payload.set_intro: In a laboratory study, 80 students watched the same short video of a minor bicycle accident. Afterward, students were randomly assigned to read one of two written summaries of the video. The summary for half of the students (the Accurate group) described only what the video showed. The summary for the other half (the Misleading group) also mentioned a red helmet, although no one in the video wore a helmet. One week later, all students answered a recall questionnaire. The table shows the results.

columns: Students who said the rider wore a red helmet

items.stem: Which concept is best illustrated by the students who recalled a helmet that was not in the video?

options.why: Misleading information introduced after an event can alter memory of the event.
Context-dependent memory concerns retrieval in the same environment as encoding.
Proactive interference concerns old information disrupting new learning.
The serial position effect concerns memory for items by position in a list.

items.explanation_en:
The correct answer is Misinformation effect. Misleading information introduced after an event can alter memory of the event.
Context-dependent memory is incorrect: Context-dependent memory concerns retrieval in the same environment as encoding.
Proactive interference is incorrect: Proactive interference concerns old information disrupting new learning.
Serial position effect is incorrect: The serial position effect concerns memory for items by position in a list.
